name: Threshold Skin
description:
Released in 2219 as a neural-feed-exclusive composition by the artist collective known as Pale Drift — a loose group of BCI engineers, composers, and neuroscientists — Threshold Skin is designed to be experienced only through direct neural interface and cannot be meaningfully translated to conventional audio. The piece operates in three simultaneous perceptual layers: a conventional musical layer audible to anyone with a basic BCI, a second layer of synesthetic color-motion hallucination accessible only to users with mid-grade sensory augmentation, and a third layer that requires military-grade sensory chrome and delivers a full-body proprioceptive experience described by reviewers as 'the feeling of being on the exact edge of a decision you cannot undo.' The piece runs twenty-two minutes and was composed using an AI trained on recorded BCI emotional states donated by three hundred volunteers.

The subject matter — the experience of loving someone across the organic/synthetic divide, the specific tenderness and alienation of touching a hand that is partly chrome — made it an immediate sensation in communities where human-synthetic relationships are common. It has been called the first genuinely new love song format in a generation: not because of what it says, but because of what it makes you feel in your own nervous system while it says it.
creator: Pale Drift (collective: Soren Mwangi-Holt, Ife Andersson-Cruz, Dasha Reinholt-Okafor)
genre: neural ambient, BCI love composition, synesthetic electronic
audience: BCI-augmented listeners across Tiers 2-5, human-synthetic couples, augmentation enthusiasts, neuroscience researchers, underground club patrons with high-grade chrome
cultural_impact: Threshold Skin forced a public conversation about what music actually is in an era of direct neural delivery — whether a composition that bypasses the ear entirely is still music, or something that needs a new name. It is frequently cited in debates about BCI consent and emotional manipulation, since the line between 'art that makes you feel something' and 'technology that induces feelings' is genuinely unclear at the third perceptual layer. It has also become something of an unofficial anthem for human-synthetic couples, who describe it as the only artwork that accurately represents their emotional experience.
story_hooks: Someone has stripped the third perceptual layer from Threshold Skin and is selling it as a standalone 'emotional induction tool' — effectively a mood-manipulation drug delivered via neural feed, and the legal and ethical status of this is completely uncharted.

A Spire-tier corporation wants to acquire the Pale Drift collective's AI training data — three hundred people's donated emotional states — claiming the donation agreement gives them rights. The donors disagree.

A character experiences Threshold Skin for the first time after the death of a synthetic partner and finds that the piece's emotional content is, for them, no longer love but something that has no name yet.
